name: dev-server-single-instance
description: "Only ONE dev server may run — the Replit workflow owns port 5000; a competing `npm run dev` causes duplicate Vite HMR servers → token clash → runtime-error overlay"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6e1994a2-ab44-499f-a89c-70d0de5c060a
---

The Replit workflow ("Start application" in `.replit`, `waitForPort=5000`) runs the single dev server (`npm run dev` → `tsx server/index.ts`) and auto-restarts it if port 5000 goes down. **Do NOT start your own `npm run dev` in the background** — you then have TWO Vite dev servers, each with its own HMR token. The client served by one instance fails the token check against the other's HMR WebSocket → `HTTP 400` on `ws://…/?token=…`, Vite falls back to a malformed `ws://localhost:undefined`, which throws a `SyntaxError` caught by `@replit/vite-plugin-runtime-error-modal` → the "runtime error plugin" overlay the user sees. This looks like "the app doesn't work" but is purely a dev-HMR artifact (production has no HMR).

**Why:** I caused exactly this on 2026-07-11 by killing the workflow's server and launching my own via Bash to pick up a `server/routes.ts` change; the workflow restarted its own too → two instances.

**How to apply:**
- To test, drive the workflow's server on `http://localhost:5000` (and the external `$REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN`). Client edits hot-reload through it automatically.
- Server-file edits (`server/*.ts`) need a restart, but `tsx` doesn't watch. To restart cleanly: `pkill -9 -f "tsx server/index.ts"` and let the workflow auto-restart ONE instance (verify with `pgrep -fc "tsx server/index.ts"` → must be `1`). Never leave a second one running.
- Diagnose HMR: check `pgrep -fc "tsx server/index.ts"`; a healthy client logs `[vite] connected`. Related: [[checkout-redesign-handoff]].

Task (2026-07-10, branch feat/property-dashboard-redesign): app loads slow + user wants flawless no-reload page transitions with skeleton loading.

**Diagnosis (done):**
- Root cause of slow load: `vite.config.ts` manualChunks catch-all `return "vendor"` merges ALL remaining node_modules into one 3.57 MB (1.09 MB gz) `vendor-*.js` that index.html loads eagerly. It contains @react-pdf + yoga (only used by dynamically-imported report generators — the careful code-splitting in [[report-gen-integration]] was defeated), recharts, stripe, capacitor.
- Page-to-page "reload" feel: routes are lazy; first visit to a page shows full-screen `PageLoader` spinner (Suspense fallback) instead of a transition. No hard `window.location.href` navs in active pages (only old merchant-terminal-mobile.tsx, which is unrouted; v2 only uses it for logout).
- Dashboards render $0/zeros while queries load — no skeletons.
- BottomNavigation already wraps setLocation in startTransition; PageTransition uses framer-motion AnimatePresence mode="wait" keyed on location.

**Plan / progress:**
1. ✅ Diagnose (above)
2. ✅ Chunking fixed — eager payload 1,271 kB gz → 203 kB gz (-84%). Three changes:
   - vite.config.ts: dropped catch-all `return "vendor"`; pinned ONLY virtual helpers (`commonjsHelpers` + `\0vite*`) to a tiny eager "helpers" chunk. Gotcha 1: unpinned, commonjsHelpers lands inside a big lazy chunk and every chunk then eagerly imports it. Gotcha 2: a blanket `\0` match drags ?commonjs-proxy libs (pako/qrcode/brotli) into the eager chunk — must stay narrow. Gotcha 3 (concurrent session found): pinning @react-pdf's dep tree to a manual vendor-pdf chunk re-eagered it because shared tiny deps (tslib etc.) got merged in; leave it unassigned instead.
   - landing-page.tsx: `LandingRuntime` (pulls three.js ~1.2MB min = 176 kB gz) now dynamic-imported in useEffect; markup paints instantly, 3D rig attaches after. Entry chunk 795→124 kB.
   - savePdf/@react-pdf (487 kB gz) now loads only on report export; landingRuntime only on landing page.
3. ✅ Seamless navigation: App.tsx `useRoutePreload` warms ~19 route chunks sequentially on requestIdleCallback (1s head start), gated to authenticated users so marketing visitors don't download the app. Dock nav already used startTransition. Also sw.js (client/public + root public copies): /assets/* now cache-first (content-hashed = never stale) → instant repeat visits; other statics stay network-first.
4. Skeleton loading states for retail/property/trades dashboards
5. Rebuild + verify chunk sizes and transitions

Note: another session is working concurrently on this repo (finished report-gen Task #59, edited vite.config.ts alongside me).

content.text:
Found it and fixed it. Here's the full picture:

## Root cause of the crashes/timeouts — two stacked defects

**1. The server was killing itself on any stray async error.**
`server/port-manager.ts:171` had `process.on('unhandledRejection', → gracefulShutdown → process.exit)`. With ~6,800 lines of routes, any single rejected promise that escaped a try/catch (a flaky Neon query, a Windcave fetch, a webpush send) took down the **entire app**.

**2. Nothing brought it back.**
I proved this empirically: killed the tsx process and the Replit workflow **never restarted it** — port 5000 stayed dead 5+ minutes (the old memory note claiming auto-restart was wrong; I've corrected it). So one bad request = app down until you press Run = the "crashing / timing out" you keep seeing.

## Fixes applied (all `tsc`-green, uncommitted)

- **`server/port-manager.ts`** — `unhandledRejection` now logs loudly and never exits. `uncaughtException` stays alive in dev, still exits in production (autoscale replaces it there).
- **`server/index.ts:245`** — error middleware no longer re-`throw err` after responding; guards `headersSent`, logs `[EXPRESS_ERROR]`.
- **`.replit`** — the Start application workflow now wraps `npm run dev` in a `while true; … sleep 2` supervisor loop, so even a genuine crash self-heals in ~2 seconds.

## Verified

- Synthetic unhandled rejection fired at the real shutdown handlers → **process survives** (previously it exited).
- Server boots in ~2s, DB verified, all routes (`/`, `/login`, `/dashboard`, `/property`, `/trades`) render headlessly with zero page errors and no runtime overlay.
- Everything else checked out clean: API responses are 2–260ms, external domain fine, no OOM kills, memory healthy.

## One action for you

The app is currently running from a stopgap instance I started (single instance, verified). **Press Stop → Run once** so the workflow takes over with the new supervisor loop — its port manager will cleanly SIGTERM my instance and claim port 5000, no conflict.
